column3: The Hebrew leaves Ruth unnamed and has no separate “One day.” BSB supplies both her name and that introductory time expression.
The Hebrew says she “was with” his young women; BSB explicitly says she had been working with them.
The Hebrew says to anoint herself and put on her clothes; BSB specifies “perfume” and “best clothes.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB identifies her as Ruth.
The Hebrew says Boaz’s “heart was glad”; BSB renders this as being “in good spirits.” It leaves the woman unnamed and calls the heap simply “the heap,” where BSB supplies Ruth and “of grain.”
The Hebrew calls the startled person “the man”; BSB supplies Boaz.
The Hebrew repeats “your maidservant,” where BSB uses “your servant” and then “me.” The word for spreading his “wing” is rendered “the corner of your garment” in BSB.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies Boaz. It lists “poor” before “rich,” reversing BSB’s order, and speaks of going after the young men rather than running after them.
The Hebrew says “all the gate of my people” knows; BSB renders this communal image as “all my fellow townspeople.”
The Hebrew first says “if he will redeem you”; BSB explicitly makes this “if he wants to redeem you.” In the second condition the Hebrew itself explicitly names willingness.
The Hebrew says she rose before a man could recognize his companion; BSB changes this to anyone else recognizing her. The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies Boaz.
The Hebrew says he measured six of barley and placed it on her; BSB says he “shoveled six measures” into the shawl. The unit and the second reference to the shawl are supplied in BSB.

The Hebrew literally asks “Who are you, my daughter?”; BSB renders the question as “How did it go, my daughter?” It supplies the names Ruth, Naomi, and Boaz where the Hebrew leaves the women unnamed and calls him “the man.”
The Hebrew names six of barley without specifying the measure and says not to return “empty”; BSB supplies “measures” and expands this to “empty-handed”.
The Hebrew’s command is “sit”; BSB uses “Wait” and supplies Naomi as speaker. The matter literally “falls,” rendered “things go” in BSB.
